title: CHAPTER                                      PAGE
summary: I A STRANGE RIDDLE is a collection of short stories and short stories. The first chapter is titled "The Secret of the House" The second chapter is called "The Crimes of the Criminals" The third and final chapters are titled "XXVII THE DISAPPEARANCE OF TRANTER"

title: CHAPTER I
summary: Monsieur Victorien Dupont appeared at the door of John Tranter's house. He was a Privy Councillor of France. The object was to return to the man who had saved his life. After a year's work, he found half the answer. The other half is in London, and he was in London to find it.

title: CHAPTER II
summary: George Copplestone had a twisted sense of the dramatic, and twisted things were expected from him. Five amazed people were awaiting further developments. Mrs. Astley-Rolfe was a charming widow of twenty-seven. She had gambled on her late husband's probable lease of life. She was in the throes of a wild attachment to George Copllestone.

title: CHAPTER III
summary: Copplestone knelt beside her, calling her by name in a strange excess of fear. The theatrical manager tore a flask from hispocket, and administered its contents freely. The spirit revived her. They lifted her gently, and laid her on a couch. Monsieur Dupont discovered, to his cost, the truth of his remark that the house was surrounded by crooked paths.

title: CHAPTER IV
summary: The Reverend Percival Delamere was rushing towards the house as if theentire penalties of sin were at his heels. Monsieur Dupont, the financier, found the body of Miss Manderson in the street. The danseuse had recovered consciousness, and was crying hysterically. She had been murdered by a brute. The four men remained, facing each other over the dead body.

title: CHAPTER V
summary: Detective-Inspector Fay was an able and successful officer. His bag had included many famous law-breakers. He was admitted to be one of the most skilful and reliable of Scotland Yard's unravelers of mystery. The inspector could not suppress his horror and indignation when the mutilated body of Christine Manderson was uncovered.

title: CHAPTER VI
summary: The inspector closed the door behind him. "Why are you here--in this house?" he demanded softly. "A riddle," Monsieur Dupont answered, in an equally low tone. "Is there any connection between the crime and your so-called 'riddle'?" Monsieurs Dupont's gigantic form seemed to acquire a new, strange, solemnity. He whispered: "A Destroyer who strikes with neither fear nor compunction--and passes on without pity or remorse"

title: CHAPTER VII
summary: "Mr. Tranter," said the inspector, "I understand that you were the last person to see Miss Manderson alive" "I believe I was," Tranters replied. "We strolled away from the house together, in the direction of theriver. The events of the evening seemed to have upset her very much, and she was nervous"

title: CHAPTER VIII
summary: "Madam," said the inspector, placing a chair for her, "I need only to trouble you with one or two questions" "I hope you will," she said fervently. "Please ask me any questions you like." "I will answer them all," the inspector said.

title: CHAPTER IX
summary: The danseuse was in a condition of the utmost distress. "I ken nothin' o' the creeme!" she sobbed. "He said to me something that made me angry," she replied. "Then it rain, and I overtook him," she said.

title: CHAPTER X
summary: The financier was extremely agitated, and tried to shake hands with the inspector. "Please leave me your address, in case I should want to ask you any further questions," the inspector said. "I stayed vere I vath--until the rain commenthed," he said.

title: CHAPTER XI
summary: "Mr. Delamere," said the inspector, "you discovered the body?" "I did," replied the clergyman, with a shiver. "I saw something white on the ground in one of the lightning flashes, and went to see what it was" The body was never found.

title: CHAPTER XII
summary: "My God!" exclaimed the manager, "what an appalling business!" "She was to have appeared at my theater, too," said the inspector shortly. "Apparently no one saw him in the garden except yourself." "I met the Frenchman, Monsieur Dupont, a little way from the river--but he had not seen him."

title: CHAPTER XIII
summary: Monsieur Dupont overheard a conversation between Christine Manderson and Inspector Fay. The conversation took place in the garden of Manderson's home. The inspector, Tranter, heard it, too, but did not know what it was about. Monsieur: "The moment I entered that house to-night I knew it was a house of sin"

title: CHAPTER XIV
summary: George Copplestone emerged from the house in a half-dazed condition. The Rev. Percival Delamere and the theatrical manager arrived shortly afterwards. Monsieur Dupont and Inspector Fay were shown to the spot where the body was found. They found a pencil in the ground at the exact spot.

title: CHAPTER XV
summary: James Layton was a builder of men in the East End of London. He denied himself anything beyond the barest necessities of existence. He read and smoked in a hard wicker chair, destitute even of a cushion. He ate sparingly, of food scarcely better than that on his neighbors.

title: CHAPTER XVI
summary: "Mademoiselle," he said, "your friend is in great danger. If you do not come with me, you will not be able to help him" "My name's Jenny West," she said, comprehending the request. "Are you willing to follow my instructions without question--to save this innocent man?"

title: CHAPTER XVII
summary: Solomon Gluckstein, original and seniorrepresentative of John Brown & Co., Jermyn Street, was particularly fond of pink. He was extremely susceptible to deshabille. Whiskey-and-soda, prepared for him in sufficient strength by his charmingdebtor, increased the fondness and the susceptibility.

title: CHAPTER XVIII
summary: Inspector Fay entered the room at one end a few seconds after Mr. Gluckstein left it at the other. Mrs. Astley-Rolfe greeted him in a friendly fashion. "I trust you have recovered from the shock of the crime," he said. "It was certainly a most disgusting crime," the inspector agreed.

title: CHAPTER XIX
summary: Inspector Fay left the house of the lady in pink. At the corner of the street he hailed a taxi and drove to Scotland Yard. Under the watchful eyes of his escort, James Layton awaited him. "I said that rather than allow Miss Manderson to be engaged to George. Copplestone, I would tear her to pieces with my own hands"

title: CHAPTER XX
summary: Oscar Winslowe's wife was the exact opposite to him, a gentle, delicate girl. He married her for her money, and treated her abominably. Monsieur Dupont became friendly with her partly because of the pity I felt for her. He undertook to watch her entry into motherhood. The madness returned when she gave birth to her child.

title: CHAPTER XXI
summary: Doctor Lessing returned to the Savoy with a letter for Monsieur Dupont. The letter contained the address of a girl, 16, who had just moved into a house in Streatham. The girl's father had been charged with her murder, and was being held in custody for a week.

title: CHAPTER XXII
summary: Tranter set off to the Crooked House in the evening, and the roads were empty. He crept under cover of the trees, and skirted the lawns to the back of the house. There, also, darkness reigned. Tranter tried to force a way through the hedge, but everywhere it was impassable.

title: CHAPTER XXIII
summary: George Copplestone was not pleased to see Mrs. Astley-Rolfe. She sat down opposite to him uninvited. "I told a lie to save you," she said, "and I expect you to be grateful" He sprang up, and stood over her with clenched hands, his face torn with fury.

title: CHAPTER XXIV
summary: A woman saw a white, pasty face that seemed to gleam at her from the darkest corner of the room. The face was the drawn pallid face, and dull lifeless eyes, of a white-haired man. "His name is Oscar Winslowe," he said fiercely. "He is my father." "Can he hear you?" she gasped. "Perhaps he can"

title: CHAPTER XXV
summary: "Forgive me," she said gently. "I would not have said what I did if I had even thought ... of that" He put a hand on her shoulder, and leant heavily on her. "Her memory intoxicates me still," he said. "My God, how I care!" she cried recklessly.

title: CHAPTER XXVI
summary: James Layton was arrested for the murder of Christine Manderson. He was seen lurking in the garden at the time of the crime. A strange message of hope, brought to him by Jenny West aroused his curiosity. "It will not be the first time I have stood before God," he said.

title: CHAPTER XXVII
summary: Monsieur Dupont sat in his room at one o'clock waiting for Tranter. A small army of workmen swarmed over the whole place in a feverish energy. For the first time since his arrival in London fear found a place in his face. Monsieur dupont almost ran to the open front door.

title: CHAPTER XXVIII
summary: Inspector Fay was occupied with the arrangement of the evidence to be presented at the inquest on the body of Christine Manderson. Monsieur Dupont called forth a smile of complacent triumph. "There is not a moment to lose. You must come with me," he said.

title: CHAPTER XXIX
summary: Monsieur Dupont tells of the murder of Colette d'Orsel, the most beautiful woman in France. "It was obviously done in the madness of jealousy and revenge," he says. "If I have the one, I am made a member of a Royal Society," he said.

title: CHAPTER XXX
summary: Monsieur Dupont was a French police officer. He was investigating the murder of two women in Nice, France. The brother of his wife had been one of the party at the time of the crime. Dupont followed scent after scent, following trail after trail, until he found his quarry.

title: CHAPTER XXXI
summary: "I am the Destroyer! I was born to kill," said the voice. "I had never seen a really beautiful woman before I saw Colette d'Orsel" "I felt no remorse at what I had done--only a sense of impersonal regret at the death of an innocent woman and a detached pity for her misfortune in crossing my path"

title: CHAPTER XXXII
summary: Four more figures dashed out through the curtains. The inspector and Monsieur Dupont joined them. Guided by the sounds in front of them, they dashed across the garden. A black wall of earth loomed up before them, like the rising of a gigantic wave. It was the beginning of the end.

title: CHAPTER XXXIII
summary: John Tranter was the son of Oscar Winslowe. George Copplestone was born into the shadow of his father's excesses. Doctor Lessing asked Monsieur Dupont about his involvement in the case. "My connection with the whole business," he replied, "is a long story"

title: CHAPTER XXXIV
summary: Half-an-hour later, when the doctor's statement had been made, Copplestone and Mrs. Astley-Rolfe stood together in the flower-laden garden. "My dear," said the new man, "I brought you here to witness my relentlesslydeliverance"
